objective_pt: Switch register on purpose: say the same thing to a friend and to a client ("Can you send it over?" vs "Would you be able to forward it?"), choosing the right verbs, phrasal verbs and openers.

teacher.goal_pt: Raise awareness that the same request changes shape with the listener.
prompts: How would you ask your best friend to lend you some money?
And how would you ask your bank manager for a loan?
watchFor: Using "I want" for requests, which sounds demanding in English.
Being too formal with friends ("Would you be so kind...") as a joke-free default.

exercises.prompt: Would you be able to send me the report by Friday?
accepted: Would you be able to send me the report by Friday?

options: I'd appreciate it if you could get back to me.
Let me know what you think.
I look forward to hearing from you.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Let me know" is relaxed and friendly. The other two are typical of formal emails.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this politely to a client: "Eu quero uma cópia do contrato."
accepted: I'd like a copy of the contract
I would like a copy of the contract, please
Could I have a copy of the contract?
Could I have a copy of the contract, please?
Could you send me a copy of the contract?
Would it be possible to get a copy of the contract?
Would you be able to send me a copy of the contract?
Could you possibly send me a copy of the contract?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "I want" sounds demanding in a request, especially to a client. Use "I'd like" or "Could I have...?".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'd like a copy of the contract, please.

teacher.goal_pt: Pair informal phrasal verbs with their formal Latin-based equivalents: find out / ascertain, get in touch / contact, put off / postpone.
prompts: What's the formal word for "put off"?
Would you write "kids" in a report?
watchFor: Assuming the Latin-based word is always better: in speech it can sound stiff.
"Postpone" vs "anticipate": "antecipar" a meeting is "bring forward", not "anticipate".

exercises.example_en: Can we bring the meeting forward to Monday?
I'll get in touch with you next week.
We are trying to ascertain the cause of the delay.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each informal phrase with its formal equivalent.
Say this in natural English: "Podemos antecipar a reunião?"
accepted: Can we bring the meeting forward?
Could we bring the meeting forward?
Can we bring forward the meeting?
Could we bring forward the meeting?
Can we move the meeting up?
Could we move the meeting up?
Can we move the meeting earlier?
Could we have the meeting earlier?
Can we hold the meeting earlier?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Anticipate" means "prever, esperar". To "antecipar" a meeting is "bring it forward" or "move it up".
commonErrors.correction_en: Can we bring the meeting forward?

teacher.goal_pt: Notice how informal speech uses reductions (gonna, wanna, kinda) and formal speech keeps full forms.
prompts: Say "I'm going to call him" quickly to a friend.
Now say it in a formal presentation.
watchFor: Over-articulating every word in casual speech, which sounds robotic.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat casually, as you would to a friend ("gonna", "wanna").
exercises.prompt: I'm gonna grab a coffee. Wanna come?
accepted: I'm gonna grab a coffee. Wanna come?
I'm going to grab a coffee. Want to come?
I'm going to grab a coffee. Do you want to come?
I'm gonna grab a coffee. Do you wanna come?

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat clearly, in a formal register.
exercises.prompt: I would be grateful if you could assist us.
accepted: I would be grateful if you could assist us
I'd be grateful if you could assist us

options: A chat with a colleague at lunch
exercises.explanation_pt: "Gonna" is normal in relaxed speech. In interviews and speeches, "going to" sounds more appropriate.

teacher.goal_pt: Identify register from a short message and reply in the same register.
prompts: Who do you think is speaking, and to whom?
watchFor: Replying to an informal message with a stiff formal sentence.
Missing that "I was wondering if..." is a polite request, not a question about the past.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What is the relationship between the speakers most likely to be?
exercises.listen: I was wondering whether you might have a moment to go over the figures before the board meeting.
options: Colleagues in a fairly formal workplace
exercises.explanation_pt: "I was wondering whether you might..." and "board meeting" signal a polite, professional register.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. A friend is asking. Reply informally that you can't tonight but tomorrow works.
exercises.listen: Hey, fancy grabbing a drink tonight?
accepted: I can't tonight, but tomorrow works
Can't tonight, but tomorrow works
I can't tonight, but how about tomorrow?
Can't tonight. How about tomorrow?
Not tonight, but tomorrow's good
Not tonight, but tomorrow works for me
I'd love to, but not tonight. Tomorrow?
Sorry, I can't tonight. Tomorrow?
Tonight's no good, but tomorrow works
I can't make it tonight, but tomorrow's fine

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Grammatically fine, but far too formal for a friend. Keep it light: "Can't tonight, but tomorrow works."
commonErrors.correction_en: Can't tonight, but tomorrow works.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Funciona" for a plan is "works" or "is good", not "functions".
commonErrors.correction_en: Can't tonight, but tomorrow works.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. A client is asking. Reply formally that you will look into it and get back to them.
exercises.listen: Could you tell me why my order hasn't arrived yet?
accepted: I'll look into it and get back to you
I'll look into it and get back to you shortly
Let me look into that and get back to you
I'll look into this and get back to you as soon as possible
I'll check and get back to you as soon as possible
I'll find out and get back to you
I'll look into it and contact you shortly
I'll investigate and get back to you
Certainly, I'll look into it and get back to you

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Dar um retorno" is "get back to you". "Return to you" sounds like you physically come back.
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll look into it and get back to you.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In conversation, "verificar" is usually "check" or "look into". "Verify" means "confirm that something is true" and sounds technical.
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll look into it and get back to you.

teacher.goal_pt: Role-play the same situation twice, first with a friend, then with a client.
prompts: You need to cancel a plan. Tell me as your friend.
Now tell me as your client.
What did you change, and why?
watchFor: "Return to you", "anticipate the meeting", "I want" in requests.
Mixing registers in one sentence ("Hey, I would be most grateful...").

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this formally to a client: "Infelizmente, vamos ter que adiar a reunião."
accepted: Unfortunately, we'll have to postpone the meeting
Unfortunately, we will have to postpone the meeting
Unfortunately, we're going to have to postpone the meeting
I'm afraid we'll have to postpone the meeting
I'm afraid we will need to postpone the meeting
Unfortunately, we'll need to postpone the meeting
Regrettably, we'll have to postpone the meeting
Unfortunately, we'll have to reschedule the meeting

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Adjourn" means to pause or end a meeting that has started. "Adiar" (move to a later date) is "postpone" or "reschedule".
commonErrors.correction_en: Unfortunately, we'll have to postpone the meeting.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Put off" is correct but informal. For a client, "postpone" fits better.
commonErrors.correction_en: Unfortunately, we'll have to postpone the meeting.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this informally to a friend: "Me avisa se você precisar de alguma coisa."
accepted: Let me know if you need anything
Just let me know if you need anything
Give me a shout if you need anything
Shout if you need anything
Tell me if you need anything
Let me know if you need something
Text me if you need anything

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Avisar" is "let (someone) know" or "tell". "Advise" means "aconselhar" and sounds very formal.
commonErrors.correction_en: Let me know if you need anything.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Precisar de" is just "need": "if you need anything".
commonErrors.correction_en: Let me know if you need anything.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a polite formal request.
accepted: I was wondering if you could help me

exercises.instruction_pt: Leave two short voice messages: first to a friend, then to a client.
exercises.prompt_en: You can't make it to an appointment tomorrow. Leave one voice message for a close friend and another for an important client, explaining and suggesting a new time.
guidelines_pt: Friend: relaxed openers ("Hey!"), contractions, phrasal verbs.
Client: "I'm afraid...", "Would it be possible to...?", "I apologise for any inconvenience."
Suggest a new time in both messages.
Close appropriately: "Cheers!" vs "Many thanks, and apologies again."

teacher.goal_pt: Check the learner can upgrade or downgrade the register of a sentence on demand.
prompts: Make this formal: "Can you help me out?"
Make this informal: "I shall contact you."
watchFor: False friends: advise, anticipate, verify, adjourn.

exercises.instruction_pt: Make this more formal and say it: "Can you help me out?"
accepted: Could you assist me?
Would you be able to assist me?
Would you be able to help me?
Could you possibly help me?
I was wondering if you could help me
I was wondering if you could assist me
I'd be grateful if you could help me
I would be grateful for your assistance
Would you mind helping me?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Help me out" is the informal version. Use "assist", "Would you be able to..." or "I was wondering if...".
commonErrors.correction_en: Would you be able to assist me?

exercises.instruction_pt: Complete the formal email ending with one word.
exercises.sentence: I look forward to ___ from you.
accepted: hearing

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so it's followed by "-ing": "hearing from you".
commonErrors.correction_en: I look forward to hearing from you.

exercises.explanation_pt: "Bring forward" (or "move up"). "Anticipate" means to expect or predict.

exercises.prompt: Please don't hesitate to get in touch if you have any questions.
accepted: Please don't hesitate to get in touch if you have any questions
Please do not hesitate to get in touch if you have any questions

practice.example_en: I'll forward you the client's email in a minute.

practice.meaning_pt: assim que for possível para você (formal)
practice.example_en: Please reply at your earliest convenience.
Don't worry, we'll sort it out tomorrow.
I'm writing regarding your recent order.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat in a formal, steady tone.
practice.prompt: I'm writing to enquire about the position you advertised.
accepted: I'm writing to enquire about the position you advertised
I'm writing to inquire about the position you advertised
I am writing to enquire about the position you advertised

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat casually, as if talking to a friend at work.
practice.prompt: Hey, got a sec? I need to run something by you.
accepted: Hey, got a sec? I need to run something by you
Hey, got a second? I need to run something by you

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: Please find the revised proposal attached.
accepted: Please find the revised proposal attached
Please find attached the revised proposal

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat in a relaxed, informal tone.
practice.prompt: No worries, I'll sort it out tomorrow.
accepted: No worries, I'll sort it out tomorrow
No worries, I will sort it out tomorrow

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: We regret to inform you that the event has been cancelled.
accepted: We regret to inform you that the event has been cancelled
We regret to inform you that the event has been canceled

practice.instruction_pt: Say this politely to a client: "Você poderia me enviar a fatura?"
accepted: Would you be able to send me the invoice
Could you possibly send me the invoice
Would you mind sending me the invoice
I'd be grateful if you could send me the invoice
Could you send me the invoice, please
Would it be possible to send me the invoice
Would you be so kind as to send me the invoice
Could you please send me the invoice
Would you be able to forward me the invoice

commonErrors.explanation_pt: After modal verbs, use the bare infinitive: "Could you send", not "Could you to send".
commonErrors.correction_en: Could you send me the invoice, please?

practice.instruction_pt: Say this informally to a friend: "Vou me atrasar uns dez minutos."
accepted: I'm gonna be about ten minutes late
I'm going to be about ten minutes late
I'll be about ten minutes late
I'm running about ten minutes late
Running ten minutes late
I'm running ten minutes late
Gonna be ten minutes late
I'll be ten minutes late or so
I'm gonna be like ten minutes late

commonErrors.match: \b(i will|i am going to|i am gonna) delay\b
commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Me atrasar" is "be late" or "run late". "Delay" is for things: "the flight was delayed".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm running about ten minutes late.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this formally to a hotel: "A gente queria saber se vocês têm vaga para março."
accepted: We were wondering whether you have availability in March
We were wondering if you have any availability in March
We'd like to know whether you have availability in March
We'd like to enquire whether you have availability in March
We'd like to enquire about availability in March
We were wondering if you have any vacancies in March
Could you let us know whether you have availability in March
We would like to know if you have availability in March

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Months take "in": "in March".
commonErrors.correction_en: We were wondering if you have any availability in March.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this informally to a colleague you know well: "Você pode dar uma olhada nisso?"
accepted: Can you take a look at this
Can you have a look at this
Could you have a quick look at this
Can you take a quick look at this
Mind having a look at this
Got a minute to look at this
Can you check this out
Could you take a look at this
Can you give this a look

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Olhar para / dar uma olhada em" is "look at", not "look in".
commonErrors.correction_en: Can you take a look at this?

practice.instruction_pt: Make this more formal and say it: "Sorry, we messed up your order."
accepted: We apologise for the error with your order
We apologize for the error with your order
We apologise for the mistake with your order
We apologize for the mistake with your order
Please accept our apologies for the error with your order
We sincerely apologise for the error in your order
We sincerely apologize for the error in your order
We're sorry for the error with your order
Please accept our apologies for the mistake in your order

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Messed up" is too informal for a client. Use "error" or "mistake" and "apologise".
commonErrors.correction_en: We apologise for the error with your order.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. You're calling your bank. Say formally that you'd like to check the status of a transfer.
practice.listen: Hello, thanks for calling. How can I help you today?
accepted: I'd like to check the status of a transfer
I would like to check the status of a transfer
I'd like to check on the status of a transfer
I was wondering if you could check the status of a transfer
I'm calling to check the status of a transfer
I'm calling to enquire about the status of a transfer
I'm calling to inquire about the status of a transfer
I'd like to find out the status of a transfer
Could you check the status of a transfer for me, please

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "I want" sounds abrupt in a formal call. "I'd like" is more polite.
commonErrors.correction_en: I'd like to check the status of a transfer.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. A friend invites you out. Accept informally.
practice.listen: Fancy grabbing a bite after work?
accepted: Sure, sounds good
Yeah, why not
Yeah, sounds great
Sure, I'm in
I'm in
Definitely, count me in
Count me in
Yeah, I'd love to
Sounds good to me
Sure, where do you want to go
Yeah, go on then

commonErrors.explanation_pt: That is too formal for a friend. Keep it casual: "Sure, I'm in!"
commonErrors.correction_en: Sure, I'm in!

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. A client asks to reschedule. Agree formally.
practice.listen: Would it be possible to reschedule our meeting to Thursday?
accepted: Of course, Thursday would be fine
Certainly, Thursday works for me
Certainly, Thursday would suit me
Of course, that wouldn't be a problem
Certainly, that's no problem at all
Yes, of course. What time would suit you
Of course. Would the morning suit you
Certainly. Thursday would be perfect
That would be absolutely fine

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Days of the week take "on": "on Thursday".
commonErrors.correction_en: Certainly, Thursday works for me.

practice.instruction_pt: Say the same message twice: first to a close friend, then to a client.
practice.prompt_en: You need to cancel a plan you made for tomorrow. Explain why and suggest another day.
guidelines_pt: Friend version: contractions, "gonna", "Sorry, something came up".
Give the same reason in both versions.
Suggest a new day in each version.

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play: handle a client call in a formal register.
practice.scene_pt: A client calls you because a delivery is late.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Good morning, this is Laura Price from Hartwell and Company. I'm calling about our order.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Greet her formally and ask how you can help.
accepted: Good morning, Ms Price. How can I help you
Good morning, Ms Price. How may I help you
Good morning. How can I help you today
Good morning, Ms Price. What can I do for you
Good morning. How may I help you
Good morning, Ms Price. How can I be of assistance

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Em que posso ajudar?" is "How can I help you?".
commonErrors.correction_en: How can I help you?

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: We were expecting the delivery yesterday, but it hasn't arrived.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Apologise and say you'll look into it straight away.
accepted: I'm very sorry about that. I'll look into it straight away
I do apologise. I'll look into it straight away
I do apologize. I'll look into it straight away
I'm sorry to hear that. I'll look into it right away
I apologise for the inconvenience. I'll look into it straight away
I apologize for the inconvenience. I'll look into it immediately
My apologies. I'll look into it right away

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Vou ver isso" is "I'll look into it" or "I'll check", not "I'll see it".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll look into it straight away.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Thank you. When do you think we can expect it?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you'll get back to her by the end of the day with an update.
accepted: I'll get back to you by the end of the day with an update
I'll get back to you with an update by the end of the day
I'll get back to you by the end of today with an update
I'll come back to you by the end of the day with an update
I'll update you by the end of the day
I'll let you know by the end of the day
I will get back to you by the end of the day with an update

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Retornar" a call is "get back to someone" or "call someone back".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll get back to you by the end of the day.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: That's fine. I appreciate your help.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Thank her and tell her not to hesitate to call again.
accepted: Thank you. Please don't hesitate to call again
Thank you for calling. Please don't hesitate to call again
Not at all. Please don't hesitate to call again
You're welcome. Please don't hesitate to get in touch again
Thank you. Please don't hesitate to call if you need anything
My pleasure. Please don't hesitate to call again

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Hesitate" takes "to + verb": "don't hesitate to call".
commonErrors.correction_en: Please don't hesitate to call again.

practice.instruction_pt: Which opening is the most appropriate in an email to a new client?
options: Dear Mr Lee, I hope this email finds you well.
practice.explanation_pt: "Dear + title + surname" and a polite opening line are standard in formal emails.

practice.instruction_pt: Which verb is the most informal?
practice.explanation_pt: "Buy" is everyday English; "purchase" and "acquire" sound formal or technical.

practice.instruction_pt: Which is the formal equivalent of "need"?
practice.explanation_pt: "Require" is the formal version: "Do you require any further information?"

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: We look forward ___ hearing from you.
accepted: to

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Look forward to" is followed by -ing: "look forward to hearing".
commonErrors.correction_en: We look forward to hearing from you.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
accepted: for

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Thank you for" something, not "by" (a copy of "obrigado pela").
commonErrors.correction_en: Thank you for your prompt reply.

practice.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a formal request.
accepted: I would appreciate it if you could reply soon

practice.instruction_pt: Match each word with its meaning and register.
